title: ARMED ROBBERY
full_story:
An armed robbery at an Effingham hotel on Tuesday night ended with a suspect in custody thanks to a K9 track, drone surveillance, and the cooperation of several departments.

Effingham Police responded to the Days Inn at about 10:30 pm after an employee reported that a man armed with a knife had demanded the hotel’s cash drawer.  The suspect grabbed the drawer, which had an undetermined amount of cash, and fled before officers arrived.  No one was injured.

Officers reviewed hotel surveillance footage to determine which direction the suspect had gone, then deployed a police K9 to track him.  The dog recovered the cash drawer and what appeared to be clothing discarded by the suspect along the way.  A drone operated by the Effingham County Sheriff’s Office then located the suspect hiding in a makeshift encampment in a wooded area behind Boos Outlet Showroom on Avenue of Mid America.  Officers and Illinois State Police Troop 9 troopers moved in and made the arrest without incident.

The suspect was identified as Nicholas A. Courtright, 20, of Effingham.  He was taken to the Effingham County Jail and booked on Class X felony armed robbery and criminal trespass charges.  Effingham County Circuit Judge Bryan Kibler denied pre-trial release on Thursday.

Effingham Police Chief Kurt Davis praised the teamwork involved in the arrest, saying the combination of video surveillance, K9, and drone technology allowed officers to track and locate the suspect quickly while keeping both the public and responding officers safe.

title: DEJAYNES HOME CONFINEMENT
full_story:
Justin E. DeJaynes, 41, of Johnsonville, was given 30 days of jail time to be served as home confinement in a plea agreement reached Tuesday in Wayne County Court.  He pleaded guilty to a charge of driving with a revoked license.

DeJaynes was originally charged in late September.  He was given two years of probation by Associate Judge Denton W. Aud.  About $2,200 was assessed to DeJaynes in fines and court costs.

The defendant had already served 22 days at the county jail, for which he was given credit by the judge, and Judge Aud asked DeJaynes to observe a no-contact order and to avoid a Fairfield man, Terry Hixenbaugh.

In the plea agreement made with the state, three cases were dismissed for DeJaynes that included alleged charges of felony aggravated battery in a public space from March 2025, improper use of title/registration last August, and a separate charge of driving on a revoked license in September.

title: NO BODY TO MURDER
full_story:
A play titled “No Body to Murder” will be held at Nostalgia Theater, formerly the Town Theater, in downtown Flora.  The play will be held next Friday, April 10th, and Saturday, April 11th, at 7 pm each night.  This fun whodunnit takes place on a stormy night and will have you laughing along and keep you guessing.  This is a stage performance, not a murder mystery event and there will be no audience participation.

The play is directed by Stacey Earleywine and is full of amazing local talent, who will blow you away with their acting abilities.  Although this play is not a musical, it is full of great songs in between scenes.

Grab a friend and enjoy an evening out with well-known community theater members Jeremy Kohn, Jim Earleywine, Matt Lovett, Jessica Muskopf, Linda Waller, Sarah Hager, and more.

Nostalgia Theater is currently being renovated and will serve as Clay County’s home for community theater.  Not only will you be able to catch some amazing live entertainment at Nostalgia, but the building is also for rent as a venue for upcoming events, such as parties, reunions, showers, and weddings.

Nostalgia Theater operates as a 501©3 non-profit and all proceeds from the Nostalgia play performances will be used to continue the renovation of the theater.  Make plans to attend this fun performance, support the hard work these actors have put into it, and see the beautiful Nostalgia Theater building as it is being brought back to life.

Tickets are $10 each.  Tickets are on sale Wednesday through Friday at Cuttin’ Up Hair Salon, next to Nostalgia Theater.  Tickets will also be available at the door.

title: SPRING TROUT SEASON
full_story:
The 2026 Illinois spring trout fishing season will open tomorrow morning at 58 ponds, lakes, and streams throughout the state.

The spring catch-and-release fishing season, is now open.  No trout may be kept during the catch-and-release period, but anglers can keep trout after the opening of the regular season tomorrow.  The daily harvest limit for each angler is five trout.

Trout Fishing can be done at the Sam Dale Lake State Fish and Wildlife Area in Wayne County, at the Turkey Run Shelter Pond, because the trout pond continues to undergo rehabilitation.  Signs directing anglers to the temporary site will be posted.  At the Mount Vernon Game Farm Pond in Jefferson County, or at the Beall Woods Lake, at the Beall Woods State Park, in Wabash County, and the Boston Pond, at the Stephen A. Forbes State Recreation Area in Marion County.

For information about all site regulations, anglers should contact individual sites that will be stocked with catchable-size trout.  Not all sites are open for trout catch-and-release season and not all sites are open at 5 am opening day.

The Illinois Catchable Trout Program receives funding support by those who use the program through the sale of inland trout stamps.  The Illinois Department of Natural Resources stocks more than 80,000 rainbow trout each year in bodies of water where trout fishing is permitted during the spring season.  An additional 80,000 trout will be stocked for the fall trout season, which begins in October.

The spring trout season offers opportunities for families to get outdoors and enjoy fishing.  All anglers must have a fishing license and an inland trout stamp unless they are younger than 16, blind or disabled, or are an Illinois resident on leave from active duty in the Armed Forces.

Fishing licenses and trout stamps can be purchased by using a credit card online.  Visit ifishillinois.org for more information on trout seasons and other Illinois fishing opportunities.

title: CARLYLE LAKE OPENING
full_story:
Spring has arrived, and the US Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Facilities at Carlyle Lake will soon open for the 2026 recreation season.  This includes the Carlyle Lake Visitor Center, campgrounds, and fish cleaning stations, all of which enrich the visitor experience and offer recreational opportunities on public lands.

Carlyle Lake Visitor Center will be open from 9:00 am to 5:00 pm on Saturdays and Sundays starting tomorrow and going through May 24th.  Then will be open Daily from May 25th through September 7th.

Dam West Campground and Dam East-McNair Campground will opened today.  Boulder Campground will open on April 17th and Coles Creek Campground will open May 1st.

Fish cleaning stations will open in mid-April, and beaches will open closer to Memorial Day weekend, depending on weather conditions.

All USACE campgrounds at Carlyle Lake – Dam West, Dam East-McNair, Boulder, and Coles Creek are fully reservable.  Each campsite features a QR Code that visitors can scan onsite to make a reservation, if available.  Reservations can be made up to six months in advance, starting from the current day, through recreation.gov or by calling 877-444-6777.

For more information, contact the Carlyle Lake Project at 618-594-2484.

title: HPIA THREAT COULD RISE
full_story:
Detections of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) rose sharply in January and February with 15.5 million birds affected in those months.

While this is substantial, it is 56% fewer birds than at the same time in 2025.  Detections slowed in March, reflecting progress in managing the outbreak.  US egg prices subsequently eased 57% so far this year compared to last year’s high, Bernt Nelson, American Farm Bureau Federation economist, reported.

But, as spring migration season takes flight, USDA is urging farmers to be vigilant with biosecurity.  HPAI is being detected in both wild birds and domestic poultry flocks across the country, increasing the risk of exposure.

USDA biosecurity assessments provide poultry and egg farmers with resources to protect flocks and safeguard food supply.  For more information, visit the website, aphis.usda.gov.

title: STATE UNEMPLOYMENT UP
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Employment Security (IDES) announced Thursday that the unemployment rate was 4.9 percent in January, up +0.2 percentage point from December, and up +0.2 percentage point from the same month, one year ago, based on data provided by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS).  The revised December unemployment rate was 4.7 percent.

Total nonfarm payrolls increased over-the-month in January, up +18,000 (+0.3%) to 6,166,800, and the largest monthly increase since June 2023.  The December monthly change in payrolls was revised from the preliminary report, from +11,800 to +11,600.  The January payroll jobs estimate and unemployment rate reflect activity for the week including the 12th.

The industry sectors with the largest over-the-month jobs increases included: Construction (+13,500), Manufacturing (+8,400), and Trade, Transportation and Utilities (+1,800).  The industry sectors with the largest monthly payroll jobs decreases included: Private Education and Health Services (-3,500), Financial Activities (-800), and Other Services (-700).

Compared to a year ago, total nonfarm payroll jobs were up +7,900 jobs.  The industry groups with the largest jobs increases included: Private Education and Health Services (+18,300), Construction (+14,000) and Government (+2,900).  The industry groups with the largest jobs decreases included: Professional and Business Services (-12,300), Trade, Transportation and Utilities (-10,000), and Leisure and Hospitality (-3,300).  In January, total nonfarm payrolls were up +0.1 percent over-the-year in Illinois and up +0.2 percent in the nation.

The number of unemployed persons in January was 318,700, up +3.5% from December, and up +1.3% over the same month one year ago.  The labor force was almost unchanged (0.0%) from December and down -1.2% over-the-year.  The unemployment rate identifies those individuals who are out of work and seeking employment.  An individual who exhausts or is ineligible for benefits is still reflected in the unemployment rate if they actively seek work.
